Privacy Policy

Last updated: October 6, 2026

Blurly is an on-device photo editing app for Android and iOS. It lets you pick, capture, receive, blur, save, and share images from your device.

Data Collection

Blurly does not collect, sell, or share personal data with the developer. The app does not include analytics, advertising, crash reporting, account creation, or a photo-processing backend.

Photos And Camera

Blurly may ask for camera and photo/media permissions so you can:

  • Pick a photo from your device.
  • Take a photo with your camera.
  • Process the selected photo locally on your device.
  • Save the processed image to your gallery.
  • Share the processed image through your device's system share sheet.

Photos are processed on the device. Blurly does not upload your photos to a server.

If you choose to share a processed image with another app, that transfer is initiated by you through your device's system share sheet. The receiving app's own privacy policy applies after you share the image.

Local Processing

Blurly uses an on-device TensorFlow Lite model and local image processing. Image data is kept on your device unless you choose to save or share the result.

App Updates

Blurly may connect to Shorebird's update service to check for and download app updates. This update connection is used for app code updates only. Your photos are not uploaded to Shorebird or to the developer.

Shorebird states that its updater uses HTTPS to check for updates and download patches, and that it does not process, transmit, or store personally identifiable information for customers' end users. Some regions may treat IP addresses in infrastructure logs as personal data.

Shorebird security information: docs.shorebird.dev/system/security/

Data Retention And Deletion

Blurly does not maintain user accounts and does not store user photos or user data on developer servers. You can delete images created by Blurly from your device gallery or file storage using your device's normal deletion controls.

Children's Privacy

Blurly is not directed to children and does not knowingly collect personal data from children.

Changes

This policy may be updated if Blurly's features or data practices change. Any updates should be published at the same public URL used in the Google Play store listing.

Contact

For privacy questions, contact the Blurly maintainer through the project issue tracker.
